name: Mistral 7B
problem: A 7B model competitive with far larger models is wanted, but inference cost at that size is set by attention cost over long contexts and by KV-cache footprint.
mechanism: Two inference-motivated architectural choices, both stated as such in the abstract: GROUPED-QUERY ATTENTION (GQA) explicitly 'for faster inference' - it shares key/value heads across query heads, shrinking the KV cache and the per-token KV bandwidth; and SLIDING WINDOW ATTENTION (SWA) 'to effectively handle sequences of arbitrary length with a REDUCED INFERENCE COST' - bounding the attended window caps the KV cache independently of sequence length.
speedup_reported: No speedup multiplier. Capability claims: Mistral 7B v0.1 outperforms LLaMA 2 13B across all evaluated benchmarks, and LLaMA 1 34B in reasoning, mathematics, and code generation. Released under Apache 2.0, which is itself the adoption fact.
notes: ADOPTION: in-production and about as widely deployed as any open model - Apache 2.0 weights, the default local model for llama.cpp/vLLM/LMStudio, and the base of a large derivative ecosystem. VENUE NOTE: no academic venue; this is a model release report, and the arXiv comment points to the Mistral news post rather than a venue, so venue = arxiv-preprint with year = ArXiv v1 (Oct 2023). INCLUDED IN AN INFERENCE SLICE DELIBERATELY, because GQA + SWA are the two most widely SHIPPED inference-cost mechanisms of the 2023-2024 generation and they are more consequential in aggregate than most of the speculative-decoding papers here - SWA is the reason a 7B model can serve long contexts at bounded memory, and GQA is the reason its KV cache is small enough to batch. Anyone attributing decode cost to architecture should start here rather than with a speculative-decoding paper.
